description:
FILED s518e (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-17) from the B::Deparse probe (#3281: lib/B/Deparse.pm dies at load by design).

REPRODUCER (main 5c5a5679; lib/Dier.pm = `package Dier; die "nope\n";`):

    PERL5LIB=lib ./runpcl p.pl     # p.pl: my $ok = eval { require Dier; 1 } ? "ok" : "died: $@"; print $ok;

perl: STDOUT `died: nope` + `Compilation failed in require at p.pl line 1.`, STDERR empty.
PCL:  STDOUT `died: nope`; STDERR, every run:
    While evaluating the form starting at line 32, column 0
      of #P"/tmp/pcl-nocache-RUEUqi.lisp":

#2764 (completed) moved the CACHED module text to a plain-stream loader, which has no herald.  A module whose load dies never gets a cache entry, so it is loaded from a nocache temp file through LOAD each time -- the herald path #2764 removed for the cached case.  Route the nocache load through the same plain-stream loader (one loader, rule 11).  The missing "Compilation failed in require" line is TEXT only (USER ruling: exact error text is not a goal; #2764 already records it).

REACH: every `eval { require Optional::Module }` whose module dies at load -- lib/B/Deparse.pm is one (Type::Tiny, Data::Dumper $Deparse, Storable $Deparse probe it).


=== DONE (s519b) ===
Commit 2a1a2461: the uncached module load (a module whose load dies is never cached) goes through `%p-load-text-stream`, the plain-stream loader #2764 gave the cached path (rule 11: one loader), so SBCL's `While evaluating the form starting at line N ... of #P"/tmp/pcl-nocache-....lisp":` herald no longer reaches stderr when the die is caught (`eval { require Dier }`).  Guard Pl/t/module-load-die-01.t rows 5-6.  The missing "Compilation failed in require" text stays TEXT only (USER ruling; #2764).
subject: #2764 residue: a module whose load DIES is never cached, so it loads through the /tmp/pcl-nocache-*.lisp LOAD path on every run and SBCL's herald `While evaluating the form starting at line N, column 0 of #P"/tmp/pcl-nocache-....lisp":` still reaches STDERR even when the die is caught (`eval { require Dier }`)
